_comment: The audit's transport gate (scripts/audit.sh §3b). Collection HTTP goes through intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_http.py (an API) or wp_net.fetch (a page a victim would load), and the User-Agent comes from wp_ua.py. A tracked *.py file that references urllib's urlopen / build_opener, or holds a hard-coded User-Agent string, must be listed here WITH THE REASON it cannot use the shared path. The audit fails on an unlisted file and on a listed file that no longer needs its entry, so this list cannot rot. To add an entry: say what the shared transport cannot do for that call site (stream, per-call proxy, cookie jar, test seam, standalone component). 'It was easier' is not a reason.

direct_transport._comment: Files allowed to reference urllib.request.urlopen or build_opener.
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_common.py: installs the per-call timeout floor around urlopen
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_net.py: fetch() and _cors_options() are the target-page fetcher (per-call proxy, redirect recorder); wayback_save() sends a Request the Wayback guard re-scopes on every redirect hop
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_ct.py: _urlopen() is a seam tests replace, inside crt.sh's wall-clock budget and breaker
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_wayback.p: the Wayback client: bounded attempts before failover, guard-scoped User-Agent
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_wayback_e: exhaustive archive job: per-exit openers and unfloored urlscan paging
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_wayback_s: the fallback path wraps its Request with wp_wayback_guard.scope_ua
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_exits.py: builds the per-exit openers (direct, HTTP proxy, SOCKS)
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_sellers.p: streams a ~110 MB download to disk in chunks
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_container: open_blob() hands back the live response as a stream for layer reads
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_buckets.p: _RAW_OPENER refuses any redirect to a host off the raw-file allowlist
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_certkit.p: cookie-jar session opener for the login flow
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_meta.py: cookie-jar session holding the anonymous edge challenge cookie
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_quarry.py: MCP session with an injectable opener
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_serp.py: _default_fetch() loads a landing page as a click would (per-call proxy, referrer headers): a target page, not an API
standalone fallback used only when wp_net cannot be imported
direct_transport.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_psl_updat: one-shot maintenance download of the public-suffix list
direct_transport.intel_engine/tools/house_report_captures: archive image fetch with a per-call proxy and a guard-scoped User-Agent
direct_transport.intel_engine/tools/search_pivot.py: fallback used only when wp_net cannot be imported
direct_transport.intel_engine/tools/kb/push_workingbase.p: pushes case findings to the analyst's own working-base server
direct_transport.intel_engine/harness/openai_backend.py: LLM backend transport, not collection egress
direct_transport.intel_engine/BinaryPivot/tools/analyze_a: streamed binary download with a byte cap; BinaryPivot ships standalone
direct_transport.intel_engine/Engage/tools/en_forms.py: Engage ships standalone; its fetch takes a per-call proxy
direct_transport.intel_engine/IntelGraph/scripts/pele_fet: installer download of a pinned, integrity-checked tarball; IntelGraph ships standalone
direct_transport.intel_engine/IntelShare/tools/sh_misp.py: the analyst's MISP instance: its own TLS-verify toggle and client string
direct_transport.scripts/osint/sharelink_resolve.py: no-redirect opener: each hop of a share link is read without being followed
direct_transport.scripts/proxy/cti_proxy.py: the egress layer itself: the failover opener and the proxy self-test

ua_literal._comment: Files allowed to hold a hard-coded User-Agent string. Each is listed in WebPivot/references/fetch_profile.json -> ua_exceptions, or is the fallback for the default.
ua_literal.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/wp_ua.py: the one conservative fallback for the Android default
ua_literal.intel_engine/BinaryPivot/tools/analyze_a: the standalone-fallback Android default and the --ua desktop opt-in
ua_literal.intel_engine/WebPivot/tools/whois_enrich: the WHOIS client strings (RDAP and WhoisXML): owner decision
ua_literal.intel_engine/IntelShare/tools/sh_misp.py: the MISP API client string (env MISP_USER_AGENT overrides it)
